## ##Data

The problem set contains monthly unemployment rate data from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database. It includes the U.S. national unemployment rate and unemployment rates of Oregon, California, Texas, and New York. The series it contains runs from January 1976 through the most recent observation available.

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(tidyquant)
library(tidyverse)

unemp_raw = read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")
head(unemp_raw)

```

## ##Wrangling

This sections includes a summary of the unemployment dataset using many wrangling steps. The tables below show the result of this.

Summary by Region\
The table shows the mean, minimum, and maximum unemployment rates for each region.

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(tidyquant)
library(tidyverse)
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR"    ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace(
      unemployment_rate,
      date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )
head(unemp_summary)

```

Recent Summary (Since 2015)\
The table summarizes the the most recent unemployment rates by restricting data to January 2025 and forward.

```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_recent  <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2020-01-01"))
unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )
head(unemp_recent)

```

Largest Month-over-Month Increases (Excluding 2020)\
The table shows the top five (plus ties) largest month-over-month increases in unemployment rates, excluding all observations from 2020.

```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_top_increases <- unemp |> 
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)
head(unemp_top_increases)
```

Largest Month-over-Month Decreases (Excluding 2020)\
The table shows the top five (plus ties) largest month-over-month decreases in unemployment rates, excluding all observations from 2020 to avoid distortions related to COVID.

```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_top_decreases <- unemp |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)
head(unemp_top_decreases)
```

## ##Visualization

Here, I visualize the patterns in unemployment using the wrangled datasets. The plots below will show trends over time, regional differences, and patterns that exclude the COVID period.

1\. Line Plot of Unemployment Over Time: this shows the unemployment rates for each region

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +        # or geom_col(), geom_point(), etc.
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region Over Time",
       x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

2\. Faceted Line Plot by Region: this shows each region's unemployment rate, viewed separately to compare easier.

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region Over Time",
       x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

3\. Bar Chart of Mean Unemployment Rate: this shows the average unemployment rates by region, going from lowest to highest.

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(forcats)
ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = fct_reorder(region, mean_rate), y = mean_rate)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Mean Unemployment Rate by Region",
       x = "Region", y = "Mean Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

4\. Unemployment Rate (Excluding 2020): this plot was chosen to show how unemployment behaved over the years, excluding 2020 to make the trends easier to observe without the extreme pandemic spike.

```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(year(date) != 2020) 
unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- unemp_no_covid |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp_no_covid |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)
ggplot(unemp_no_covid, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region Over Time (Excluding 2020)",
       x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```
